narrative.overview: TroopToTask should feel like a field ledger translated into a modern product surface: disciplined, legible, and built for repeated operational use. The interface earns trust through alignment, rules, restrained contrast, clear labels, and fast recognition. It should feel closer to accountable paperwork and technical manuals than a generic SaaS dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink surfaces with a dark operational rail.
Operational amber used as signal, not decoration.
Condensed display type for command hierarchy, serif body copy for readable content, mono labels for metadata.
Hairline dividers, tight radii, minimal shadows, and strong alignment.
Dense controls that stay predictable under pressure.

rules.name: The Amber Is Signal Rule
rules.body: Operational amber is for selection, focus, current state, and action. If it is being used only to make a surface more exciting, remove it.

rules.name: The Paper Never Goes Pure White Rule
rules.body: Product surfaces use warm paper values, not flat white. Pure white makes the system feel generic and breaks the field-document character.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Tables, panels, and page regions should be flat until a state change or modal layer earns elevation.

rules.name: The Border Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Reach for a 1px rule, tonal background, or alignment before adding shadow.

dos: Do use warm paper surfaces, dark ink, hairline rules, and tight radii as the default visual grammar.
Do keep operational amber rare and meaningful: focus, active nav, selected state, current day, and action emphasis.
Do use mono labels for metadata, filters, breadcrumbs, table headers, badges, and operational markers.
Do make dense product controls predictable, keyboard-accessible, and visually stable across breakpoints.
Do preserve WCAG AA contrast and never depend on color alone for status.
donts: Don't create generic SaaS marketing surfaces inside authenticated workflows.
Don't use shiny startup dashboards, soft productivity-app tropes, "AI slop," or fake command-center theatrics.
Don't use decorative gradients, glassmorphism, excessive roundness, heavy glow, or purple-gradient AI aesthetics.
Don't make card soup. Use cards only for bounded items, repeated records, modals, or genuinely framed tools.
Don't use side-stripe borders greater than 1px as colored accents on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
Don't use amber as a general decoration color.
Don't animate layout or add novelty motion that does not communicate state.
